text: Great determination of nourishment things on the menu just as a pleasant choice of specialty brews. They have indoor and outside seating. The café is anything but difficult to see from the road, yet stopping is somewhat constrained. They additionally have a pastry kitchen nearby which is enjoyable to visit also. Out them an attempt.

Sadly this Bully's has really gone far downhill since owner Paul Sonner passed away in December 2009. This restaurant and sports bar looked very sharp then...The entire place now looks tarnished and dusty now. The worn flooring, the aging tables, the worn out chairs, the dusty cases housing signed jerseys on the wall, the very old television sets with very poor resolution...The bathroom tiles--these items all look like they did in 2008--almost 11 years ago...Nothing in Bully's has been refreshed...or well manintained...                                         
              For a Bully's veteran--we have been there 50+ times since 1998--this is sad to see...Also--the chow has gone way downhill--we received food that was lukewarm and mediocre--our Nachos were cold--so we sent them back. They made us another set of Nachos that were a bit warmer..                                                                                                  
             Our server was Heather--she's nice, and efficient..but when  we received our bill--Bully's tried to bill us for 2 sets of nachos--even the cold nachos that were returned uneaten...In addition--the prices are no longer a deal at Bully's--It was $5.00 for an O'Doul's near beer...I cannot recommend Bully's as a cool Reno place to go...

Okay, am I going to lose all credibility if I say that I kind of really liked Voodoo BBQ?

Let me start by saying that I am not as much as a barbecue "expert" as some other folks, but I do know what I like. We were here for dinner on a Friday night. This is one of those "order at the counter" type places and after looking over the menu, I decided to get the brisket platter with cole slaw, mac and cheese and corn bread.

I really liked it! The brisket was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor and the cole slaw was obviously fresh made. The mac and cheese was okay, but I could tell it had been made way earlier in the day and just warmed up when I ordered it. This will probably be the only thing that I skip next time. The corn bread was soft and very good. I was surprised how much I enjoyed the platter, and overall I think it's a good deal for $10.

If you are looking for fancier barbecue, then head over to Blue Oak, but if you are in the area, Voodoo will satisfy your craving

It's worth every minute of the 20+ minute wait for food here, but don't let that stop you!!! I've eaten a lot of BBQ in my life and Roper's is PERFECT!!! It was so good I visited twice in two days, having different items each time. First, the #7 half-rack of ribs was perfectly sauced, incredibly tender and the perfect pink all the way through and shows the amazing smoke technique they use. The potato salad isn't bad, too. The next day I had the #25 pulled pork sandwich. Rather than slather it in sauce and make the concept of a BBQ sandwich unusable (some places act like it's a Sloppy Joe), there's minimal sauce. And I mean minimal; the meat's the star. For flavor, they rely on a wonderful blend of savory spices. There's enough moisture to make the meat not sloppy, very tender and they don't skimp on the amount. Another bonus is they actually PULL the pork so the strands varied in length and the meat kept the moisture and tenderness needed for a sauceless sandwich. Check out ropersribs (dot com) for menu, etc. but I'd seriously call ahead and pick up your order rather than wait around/park in this area. The neighborhood isn't "desirable" but not deadly or anything. There's a semi-paved lot around the corner half a block away where everyone parks and it's clearly lighted from the road. No matter what, the food is worth the trip and the guy at the counter was incredibly pleasant and helpful.

It was a Saturday night! We are pizza fans so we were excited. When we first arrived, there was a wait so we were able to give our phone number and receive a text message when our table was ready. We were notified to come in. The ambience is very much hipster. The music was good but loud, and it was so dark that I could hardly see the menu. 
                 The table we were sat at was very tiny. The waitress gave us two water glasses and a large bottle of water. The appetizers consisted of a couple of Brussels sprouts items, bruschetta and fried chickpeas. Not your traditional items. My boyfriend and I ordered a pizza to share and was told it feeds 2 adults. When the pizza arrived it looked delicious! New York style and very thin crust. The crust tastes ok, but the pizza sauce tastes canned and bland. There weren't enough toppings. We only ate two pieces each and didn't take the rest home. But overall, not impressed and probably not coming back.

My girlfriend and I went for lunch. What a delightful and cozy restaurant in a house at the corner of Piccadilly and Manhattan.

The front porch is enclosed and has those big gas heaters. There's an enclosed back porch with the same, and an open deck.

Inside, the restaurant is maybe 12 tables with a good-sized bar.

Our server was extremely attentive and friendly.

We started with a cup of ham and bean soup ($3.99). Chili also was available. The soup was sooooo good, brimming with ham and beans, of course, but other vegetables like onion, carrots and celery.

My girlfriend got the meatloaf ($8.99), which comes with green beans and mashed potatoes & gravy.

I could not help myself (as it was my birthday) and got the half fried chicken ($9.99), which comes with green beans and mashed potatoes (I skipped the gravy.).

The food was exceedingly flavorful and home-made with all the taste of grandma's kitchen.

The green beans were just perfectly cooked with just a tad of crispness to them and well-flavored.

The mashed potatoes were great and buttery. I do so like them without gravy.

The fried chicken was so crunchy on the outside, and moist and tender on the inside. Good flavor.

I had a hefty to-vessel of three pieces of chicken, and portions of both green beans and mashed potatoes to take home.

Man, that soup really filled me up.

When we left, we were bid farewell, and our server called out "Happy Birthday!"

As soon as I got home, I found a recipe for ham and bean soup. I'm gonna make this.

I have been to this restaurant once and I will never go back due to the horrible service and mediocre food. 

I went there with a friend and our server was always very short with us and had no emotion. That's fine, I guess, if that's his personality, but the table next to us had about 10 mid-50s customers and he was super friendly and cracking jokes with them. Maybe he thought they would give him a better tip and therefore didn't give a crap about me and my friend? I don't know his reasoning, but that was just not good customer service in my opinion. I would expect to be treated the same as all of the other customers, no matter how old I may look.

My friends and I just walked out of this dump. Place was filthy from lobby to bathroom to dining area. I wouldn't eat here if they paid me to try their food. Staff seemed like zombies and was creepy. Dumpster outside was piled so high and staff smoking on side of building- possibly even meth? Do yourself a favor if you decide to come here- put your car in reverse, put "Perkins" in your GPS, and step on the gas. Gross.

In his roundup of the best Tampa Bay dining spots of 2005, the food critic for the St. Petersburg Times cited this place as having the Crust Most Likely to Make the National Register of Historic Pizzas, which lead us to give it a try. Suffice it to say I won't be trusting any of his other recommendations or future reviews. Housed in a nondescript brick building nearly lost among the body shops that surround it, this joint has been making pies for some fifty years, apparently for a lot of very non-discriminating palates. The cracker-thin crust, with the texture and taste of a stale matzoh, was barely covered with a thin layer of odd-tasting sauce and a very skimpy sprinkling of cheese. The only award I'd give it is the Pizza Most Likely to Make a Grown New York Italian Weep.

My favorite part of fall - RBW. 

In its fifth year, it has grown to 10 days. This year there is a noticeable structure change. Restaurants can offer $10, $20 and/or $30 RBW specials. And as past years, a different fabulous event.  Also new are slips that can be checked off for one of three local charities to receive a donation from RBW that Sysco funded. 

I began my kick off at Mellow Fellow, new to RBW and a spot I hadn't yet tried. (thanks to RBW for a new discovery.)Their kick off special was a bison sausage and a pint for $10. Their week long special is a stuffed burger and beer $10. 

Saturday afternoon Pignic celebrated its anniversary by hosting a Pigtoberfest.  Sausages, three sides and beer were available while listening to live polka music. 

Noble Pie offered a $10 meatballs and crispy polenta plate at both locations. 

Under the Rose hosted Blend Catering for a OktoberFeast- an Israeli family style dinner. $70 for SO much food and drink. I always enjoy Blend's participation in RBW. They are a Catering company so RBW is a special opportunity to eat their delicious food. 

Rapscallion opened its doors in 1977 and presented a one night special 5 course dinner based on it. So much old school food and a fun evening. Check out Rapscallion review for menu and pictures. 

I skipped the Tuesday night special event to dine close to home with a large group of friends at ZoZo's. Last year and this year they do RBW right. A 5 course Italian dinner for $30. Add to that a Yelp check in and receive a glass of chianti for free. So much food, wine and friends. That what ZoZo's is year around. 

Wednesday night was just wild, Yelp created a Far East event with nine Asian restaurants at the sky terrace on the Nevada art museum. What a night of fantastic Asian food and drink samples, as well as various performances. 

Moroccan food from Nicholle at Homage filled my Thursday night. Fabulous food and entertainment. Too bad the weather didn't get the same memo, it was just a bit chilly. But that didn't stop a sold out crowd from having a wonderful savory night in the spice desert. 

Friday for lunch Chris M and I braved the spitting rain and smoke to check out the yummy lamb sandwich special with fries and dessert bite at Creme for $10. Great bargain, totally full.  
The food truck wars was cancelled in the morning due to the unpredictable rain, winds and smoke of the day. 

Saturday- it's exciting and sad. It's the end of RBW, but it hosts the Chef Showdown!! An incredibly exciting free event where you can wander around Czyz's showroom and watch 8 local chefs battle it out with their unique cooking skills. This year with the help of Sysco there were small bites and beverages to be enjoyed during the event.  

I capped off my Saturday and week with a dinner and show. Brilliant combination of Tournant's Hannibal dinner paired with Good Luck Macbeth's hilarious production of Silence. 

Check out individual reviews of each business for a more detailed account of the events and meals. 

Thanks to Natasha Bourlin and Clint Jolly for starting and keeping this fabulous foodie festival going. Look forward to year six.

Steak and Eggs for $5.95, let's go!

I'm a frequent flyer here, and the main reason being...PRICE. However, with great price comes some minor "risks" as well.

The main things that I have noticed since eating here often is:
-The steak is never the same size, you might get the perfect portion or the tiniest bit, which will have you contemplating whether you should order another
-The Staff is very attentive but sometimes the service can be slow, even when the place is empty (large parties, keep that in mind)

On the bright side,
Very cozy atmosphere, when I eat here it doesn't feel like a casino at all, which I find pleasant!

Overall: A-

UPDATE: 
1. Steaks have been much more consistent, I'm very happy, cooked to order and perfection!
2. Jessica has been our usual waitress and she has provided excellent service!!

Okay so when I saw that salem's was getting a location in Brandon, I thought it was the second coming of Jesus. I was so happy. The ones in Tampa are SO GLORIOUS. I was in bliss...

Little did I know the disappointment I was about to get. 

This doesn't even seem like the same chain!!
It was not even CLOSE to as good as the ones in Tampa. 

I took my sister and my two cousins from up north for their first salem's experience and WE WERE ALL SO PSYCHED! 

My fries weren't good, the gyro had like no sauce on it, the bread was hard...COME ON ITS LIKE THEY WERENT EVEN TRYING. I looked like such an asshole bragging on this place. 

Can't say I won't go back though, it's a shorter drive for me.

This little pizza place is my new favorite comfort food go to. The pizzas are unusual, fresh, good quality, and delicious! One of my favs is the Peace in the Historic East Nashville. Instead of regular sauce, it has a hummus base, which didn't sound too appetizing until I tried it - it's amazing! Plus, they have great delivery! 

If I had one complaint, it would be that the middle eastern food has some room to grow. It doesn't seem as fresh or well sourced as pizzas and they don't have homemade sauce/dressing. However, for a delivery place, it's definitely the best I've had in Nashville.

A friend of mine recommended this restaurant to me. It took me a while to get down and try it and I regret not trying it sooner. Boy they did not disappoint. I would've taken a picture of my food but it did not last long enough. I'm very picky about my catfish and there's was very good and it came with hush puppies which I love. I also ordered a side of coleslaw it was a little different than traditional coleslaw. I think I found a new favorite spot to eat! Yum!

you know how you read a review and you think it cant really be as bad as all the other one star reviews because you have been there before, ok, so it was 20 years ago, but still.. well, believe all the one star reviews because it is all true.
we were given chips with salsa when we sat down, the waiter was very friendly.  the spicier of the two salsa's was uneatable. the mild one had no taste
i ordered a burrito, i was served a quesadilla that barely had any filling in it. i ordered a side of beans. they were the absolute worse canned beans i have ever had.
my friend order a veggie chimichanga and got the burrito( maybe it was the one i ordered)   there was one veggie in it, a piece of broccoli that was probably saved from the last time she was there, 20 years ago. she was looking for to it because when she was there 20 years ago, it was filled with all kinds of veggies, it was huge and yummy. not this time.
the bad taste this food leaves in your mouth will even linger to the next day..

By far my favorite pizza spot in Philly. I had a lot of trouble finding decent pizza in Philly when I first moved here but was lucky enough to come across their twitter account and tried it. 

A little bit on the pricey side but it is more gourmet pizza then anything else. They have some great specialty pizzas and their sauce is great. I recommend the italian sausage pizza. It is delicious!

I also have stopped by and eaten at the at the actual restaurant which has a plethora of pizza slices available that aren't on the menu.

First, I definitely recommend this place.  Though some of the food was good (sorry, we've been around) others were excellent with caveats.  Texas Joe's was excellent, a little smoke, meat and bbq was great, and the pickled onions were nice.  Not spicy or heavy on the smoke if you're into that.  Mrs. Had brisket sandwich and she was really happy.  I liked the baked beans, Mrs. Had mac and cheese which was ok.  We had cornbread which was good, but didn't have anything that differentiated it from others we had (good though).  Finally, you have to have the banana pudding which we enjoyed.

Good BBQ, which you have to try if that's on you foodie list.  Well be back, that's for sure.

Sonic, well this Sonic was not the greatest, they took for ever to get two fresh fruit slushes! I mean they dont take that long and there was not hardly anyone there. then a staff, not sure if he was off or on shift, but he and friend were BLASTING their rap music in the parking lot and being very inconsiderate of other people there. Probably wont return to this one!

Grand Buffet has been around for awhile. I've been to this suburban restaurant many times, both for lunch and dinner. It's in a large shopping center with plenty of easy parking.

Their buffet offers your typical choices, like lo mein and fried rice, is clean, and has a tasty, slightly greasified hot and sour soup that I like. Last I checked, they offered a full menu to order from, but I've never tried that. But why bother, since their buffet will feed you silly, and on the cheap which probably explains why they're usually crowded. Stop by if you're in the mood for Chinese.
so good! Share some appetizers or plates. Definitely better to experience more things! Great beer selection!

One of the must dos on any trips is a nice dinner.

However, this trip we decided the day of to make reservations of where to go.  What made this even more difficult was our group was 14 people.  Good luck finding a 5 star restaurant who could even take that reservation alone, but only a few hrs before? Slim to no chance.

We were lucky, because Herbsaint was able to accommodate our request.  When we arrived we noticed they had set up our table outside, which wasn't so bad since it was a cool night, and this way our group could be a bit louder.

I started out with the gumbo, it was OK, not the best by any means a friend got the soup of the day which was superb, don't remember what it was (sorry).  

My section of the table decided to start out with a couple of the small plates and share them so we could sample their offerings.  We got the gnocchi, the beef short rib, and the spaghetti with the fried egg.  By far the spaghetti with the fried egg was the best.  It was a bit rich but really satisfying.

As far as entrees went our section were so happy with being able to try so many dishes for appetizers we decided to do something similiar with the main dishes.  The special for this night was lamb neck, yes lamb neck.  This thing was the most amazing piece of meat I had ever tasted.  Another person in the group had the ribeye, which was OK but nothing out of this world, and another person had the pork belly, that was good but the lamb neck had just blown everything else out of the water.

The french fries with pimenton aioli sounded great so we decided to add an order of that too.  It lived up to the description.

Overall, the best dishes were the "specials" of the day.  Fast service and 2 thumbs up for being able to squeeze our large group in.

text:
If it were more consistent it could easily be a 4 star place.  They have great staff and an excellent selection of items that cover everything from the traditional to more adventurous. 

Their cookies are better than the pizza (I know - right?!). 

The garlic knots are good or dreadful - no telling.  Sometimes they are a sublime combination of garlic and bread perfectly cooked and perfectly tender.  Other times the garlic is soooo bitter they are like small acrid balls of yuck.  

Generally speaking the pizza is really good.  The last few times we have had very inconsistent sauce.  Tonight the sauce was so salty the slices were actually ruined.  This has never happened before - but lately the sauce has been of varying degrees of saltiness.  We asked a good friend about this tonight (a true devotee)  and they said they had a similar experience last week. (We decided it was the sauce and not the cheese since the marinara with the garlic knots was also too salty)

they didn't get this popular with all of these issues so I'm hoping they work out the kinks and get back to basics!

I'm reviewing this only on the lunch buffet because I know dinner service can be a completely different experience. 

The food was mediocre at best. If you are a vegetarian, don't bother with lunch here. I was surprised by the food, it had little to no taste, which everyone knows is odd for Indian. It had some spice, but it was lacking flavor. Maybe it's just the vegetarian dishes. I hope it was because people were forking it down in there. Stupid me and my vegetarianism!  Also, and I was actually quite upset by this, the gulab jamun was freezing in the middle. The sauce it was placed in was lukewarm and tasted sour.  I spit it out.

The atmosphere was terrible and the cash register is placed at the back, so as you walk in to this crowded little space you are forced to proceed all the way to the back in order to get your name on a waiting list. Why a list is necessary is beyond me.  The staff was pleasant enough and they were quick to clear plates. I don't think that was enough for me, though. I could hear every word my neighbor was saying. He went on for thirty minutes dissing his wife. Just saying, I probably shouldn't know this much about a random stranger. The tables are impossible to negotiate if you are overweight.  If you are a fat guy like me then you can plan on leaving with curry on your shorts.  Did it have bathrooms?  I don't recall and I'm not sure I want to see the inside. What's with mini-mall restaurants, Boise, seriously?!  Who decided this was a good idea?

I probably won't give this place a second chance.  The price makes it ok for one go, but the food and the subsequent stomach issues are more than adequate reason to never let this happen again.

We found it through yelp. it had good reviews and was open at mid-afternoon.  it is not peruvian, but a fusion.  

the fried mixed seafood was ok, but not great.  the fried rice as a side was $14 (!) an dwas described as 'mass'.  

the service was pleasent, but we were perhaps hot coming in and slightly grumpy. 

we did not have the doughnuts, and probably should have.  It's not 2-star, Meh, but 3-star, Meh.  I can't imagine that we will make it back.  There are places we would try when visiting Tampa.

I usually eat at Subway, and after this experience, I'll continue eating at Subway.

I walked in to a woman who was cleaning off the slicer equipment.  She greeted me and asked for my order, so I asked for a small #10 on wheat.  She continued cleaning the slicer and told me it'll be a minute.  She then pulled out a loaf of bread, cut it in half, and asked the next guy behind me for his order.  She then pulled out another loaf of bread, and started to prepare for his order in conjunction with mine.  Somehow, with the two line attendants, his order had the mayo/mustard and vegetables laid out before mine, confusing me about whose order was being prepared from the start.

When my order was thrown in the oven to be toasted, the cashier already was asking me if I was ready to ring up, to which I responded, I'm not ready  yet.  After, I had a short exchange of words with the "sandwich artists," who then informed me that the guy behind me had his order prepared first, and that my order was the one in the oven.  After going through the veggies line up, They cut and started to wrap up my order.  I briefly noticed at that time the bread was whiter than normal, and asked to confirm the sandwich bread was wheat.  Of course, it wasn't, even after I had explicitly asked for wheat bread.  They pulled out another darker brown wheat loaf and began to cut it, before  responding that they'd probably have to remake it.  I told them it's okay, that they can just transfer everything over, and I'd be fine with it.  Well, transfer they did, but they couldn't transfer the mustard or the cheese, and of course, they didn't make any attempt to replace it on the wheat loaf.

Finally, upon ringing up, I was told that my order came to a total of $9.66.  Thinking quickly, I asked how much the double meat I ordered came out to be.  They informed me double meat was $2.50 - 50% of the cost of a normal 5" small sub that would otherwise be $4.59 before tax.  Now it was $9.66.  It was doubled the cost, for just twice the serving of meat.

Overall, the team didn't get my order right because they didn't listen to me, they try to multi-task on multiple customers' orders, causing confusion in the order process for the customer, and when called out in their error, they make very little effort to fix the error.  Let alone the fact that their portions are more expensive for smaller sizes, they offer half the available veggies than Subway, and the selection of bread types is very basic.  I will never shop at Port of Subs EVER again because of this experience.

Really tasty tacos with 4 options of salsa + chili, what more do I need?
After reading about Condesa's opening, I was intrigued but wary about its potential. Mexican restaurant opened by the Suraya crew? I know they can do Lebanese but can they do Mexican justice? Via the masa, why yes, they most certainly can.
I went with my adventurous gut and it paid off.

I was greeted instantly which is always a plus --- thanks for always noticing whomever walks through the door! It was easy to be seated as I waited for my friend. Our waitress was very well versed in the ingredients and options as we debated about what to order. We decided to get the pork rinds as a snack while also choosing two taco options and an entree to share.
The pork rinds were well seasoned and perfect to use for all the salsa and chilis. They were super crispy and at times, too hard to bite, so please be warned. In terms of the salsas, I especially liked the salsa Verde which was so bright and refreshing. It's my favorite verde in the city. The chipotle and the orange spicy (a nice burn, if you're into it) are definitely not lacking. The star of the show is the habañero pickled onions. I was so obsessed that they gave us a second batch! I felt so at home with that gesture. Thanks for encouraging us to eat more :)

My favorite is the suadero chilango taco, which contains brisket and tongue. My friend was pleasantly surprised by how tender and flavorful it was. The lamb adobado was also delicious. Each order comes with two tacos so they are shareable with plenty of protein in them.

For the entree we shared the pescado veracruz which was a tender and light fish with the fresh tortillas, and a healthy salsa with grape tomatoes. Portion wise this was much smaller and lighter but you could make approximately 4 tacos out of it.
All of these options included in-house masa aka heirloom corn from Mexico that's grounded here and made into these textured tortillas. So fresh, so delicious.
Of course, we had to have the habañero onions added to everything. Needless to say, I was sniffling by the end of the meal but it was a blissful discomfort. Added with the beautiful bright and open space (albeit unfortunate location in the alleyway but who isn't open to some adventure these days?), Condesa is here to give people a real kick in the mouth. Bring on the spices, kids!

Parking: Free small lot right in front that holds about 15 cars and limited free street parking outside the lot.

Service: Hostess didnt seat us with menus which was odd, but she came over with them a little bit later. Waiter was friendly and attentive! Food took 13 minutes to come out. We did arrive on a late Saturday around 11:20am. In and out in less than an hour. 

Food: My boyfriend ordered a chai tea latte, side of grits and tofu scramble. I ordered a meat lovers frittata. Everything was fine except how less-than-warm the grits were. 

Interior: A lot of artwork and plants. Cute place with a chill vibe!

I've driven by this place countless times before giving it a try. My wife and I shared a few sushi rolls. The specialty roll we got was very tasty while the regular rolls were decent. Sushi prices were reasonable. The space is very roomy and comfortable inside. Our only complaint was the smooth jazz versions of awful pop songs (ie Richard Marx) that wore out our ears  a bit by the end of dinner. The parking lot is very small and tough to find in the dark.

Kind of a mixed bag. Pretty pricey. The guac made table side quite good  Some of the apps were pretty tasty. Our main courses were a bit disappointing. Overcooked meat. Too much sauce that wasn't appetizing. Chunky cheese accompaniment. They need to up the freshness and flavor. Less salt more quality ingredients attention to detail.

This is one hard review to do. I use to sell food to this place some years a go and me and my family have been coming here for atleast 30 years as well. Ok Her goes what we experienced. We chose a mid week night to have dinner to avoid the long lines that user to be crazy on the weekends.(I kind of doubt that's s the case any longer) We were a party of 7, we were quickly seated next to the front door, no real big deal but not a great place to sit. We figured maybe we would get great service however that was not the case. Service was just terrible, easy slow and had to beg to get like a salad after 20 minutes it would have been ok if the place was full but if wasn't by any means. The food my wife and I arrived early and decided to get a drink and a shrimp cocktail omg $7.75 got us 4 very very small shrimp like from a 21to 30 count size. But ok let's move on, the rest of the family showed up and we continued. After the crazy wait time our food started to arrive, every dish was over cooked! Some not as much as others, 5 of us decided we were to hungry to wait any more so we just started, the other two in our party just had to send back the overcooked plates back as they were un editable, bad news is that when we were all done eating their good still didn't come! I went and asked for a manner they finally sent one out I told him most of what had happened and asked that he at least go say something to my 73 old mother that still had not gotten her dinner and never did, we had them pack it up as the rest of us were done and just wanted out! They said oh we'll make it right and took off one dinner! OMG never ever again, sorry to see an old friend die!

When I'm happy, I go to Rangoon.
When I'm sad, I go to Rangoon.
When I'm in Chinatown, I go to Rangoon.
When I'm not at Rangoon, I want to be at Rangoon.

The staff is friendly, the food is great (GREAT), the prices are reasonable, and I love that they serve tea in those mugs with lids (because they steep it in your mug, not in a pot). In fact, this place inspired me to go out and buy one of those mugs for myself.

I highly recommend the Jungle dishes (Jungle Tofu, Jungle Chicken, etc.) and pretty much any other spicy dish on the menu. If you want something sweet, go with a Mango dish.

Then you'll always want to be at Rangoon, too.

I gave this a 3 star only because the woman that took my order and the delivery lady were very professional as well as very nice.
My pizza was barely lukewarm.  I did not like the taste of the pizza.  Also, the Coke I ordered was delivered warm.  When I placed this order, I asked if the soda was cold and was told that it was.  Had I known it was not cold, I would not have order Coke with this pizza.
I was disappointed with the food and will not order from Domino's again.

With the Ardmore restaurant scene booming I've been excited to see a lot of new culinary experiences finally come to the Main Line area. So when I first heard about Bam Bam Kitchen coming to my former stomping ground I was excited not only for the prospect of enjoying Korean food, I was excited for it adding another BYOB into the mix!

I give a 4 star for now since I only went during Ardmore Restaurant Week. But it gave a very suitable preview of exceptional service, quaint decor, and super delicious food. It was also cool that they had an open kitchen where you could watch the food prep, and buzzers you could use to contact the friendly servers.

The four course deal was a perfect chance to try an ample amount of things on the menu, and it started with a delectable amount of vegetables like kimchi, scallion salad, and other offerings to share. Next up was an appetizer course, and it was hard to pass up on some amazing Korean fried chicken at the highest spice level possible! For the main course it was hard to pass up on any of their delectable Korean stir frys served on a hot plate, especially since the seafood option came with shrimp, calamari, scallops, and mussels. And it had the right level of delectable spices and flavor! Dessert was on the menu as well, and it was impossible to pass up on the green tea mochi for the perfect end note.

Add in other traditional dishes like deep fried katsu, marinated prime rib galbi, bimbimbop served in a sizzling stone bowl, huge fried mandoo dumplings, and you have plenty of reasons to pay a visit!
I enjoyed it - the food was good enough and the drinks were yummy.

After reading the mixed reviews i had to try this place for myself. I order the fried wing meal, for my two sides I chose Mac N cheese and the yams. The Mac and cheese was average, the fried chicken had the perfect crispy crunch I was looking for, and the yams were delicious. The yams were actually my favorite part of the meal, made the Mac N cheese a little tastier;). Overall I thought the food was very good, I'll be going back when I get my crunchy fried chicken craving again!  Also on a side note my container was very full so the young gentleman who was cooking was nice enough to wrap my container in clear wrap. I thought that was a very nice gesture, customer service goes a long way, that's why he got a two dollar tip :D

I felt like I was hanging out on the deck of a friends house, eating home made goodness and drinking craft beers. It's that simple. 

Coll, mid-week night and we passed through the main room/bar/lounge of this little house. The vibe was totally laid back with some tables, the bar and a sofa lounge area, all filled with people eating, drinking and chatting it up. Once great thing about Santa Barbara is it's size. I love running into people I know and here, I ran into 3. All of whom were excited to hear this was my first time and told me it would not be my last. 

We sat on the back deck with a hand full of high tops. You're crammed in between the nextdoor neighbor, the kitchen wall and a small, backyard parking lot but you don't notice. It's cute, fun and filled with good music and happy people. Lights strung about provide ample, mood lighting and the heaters will keep you warm. 

Our server came out to talk up the menu, of which he was knowledgeable but he really shined with the craft beer conversation. We made our selection at his recommendation and waited for it all to arrive.

Black & Blue with garlic parm fries were killer. A hint of sweet, sticky love as they melt in your mouth.
Lamb ball sammy with salad. Moist and juicy. Easier eaten with a fork and knife to shovel this deliciousness in. 
Brussels sprouts were ok, small and wimpy. I was expecting more here and will pass on the next go round.

The gang is all young and hip, 30s and beyond, total awesomeness and all welcome. I love this crowd.

Soooo, I ordered for delivery. About an hour and ten mins wait. I ordered lamb, rice & broccoli. The broccoli was good it was a very small portion. The lamb was a little tough the teriyaki sauce tasted like some type of weak bottled sauce . $30 platter, lemonade, banana pudding. The reason I ordered from here was because the photos all look so good. Banana pudding was good, strawberry lemonade good. I feel like when you watch a fast food McDonald's commercial and u go into the restaurant and your food  doesn't look anything like the commercial. FYI can't stand McDonald's...
Bottom line did not enjoy my bogus food at all I feel like I was scammed... Out of $30 bucks!! and a tipI gave 2 stars because the guy on the phone was cool~

Perfect Neapolitan in every way.  

No meat is offered here, totally vegetarian, they do have vegan sausage.

Staff was very nice, and I heard them mention they may offer delivery in the future.  

They are going to need a bigger place because this place is going to be wildly successful.

Breakfast at Green Eggs is a stressful and confusing experience. I'll admit I was excited about the new location in midtown village when I saw the Green Eggs sign go up. The food at Green Eggs is really good and I was looking forward to adding them to my line up. However after my first visit I was quickly reminded why I don't go to Green Eggs Cafe and why I don't think I'll be back anytime soon. 

First off they have too many rules. One of the rules and regulations is that they do not allow breakfast sandwiches while you are dining inside. Egg and cheese on a croissant is one of my favorite things to get for breakfast but when I tried to order one the waitress informed me that sandwiches are only available to go. I'm assuming this rule is in place because the price for a sandwich is less than an entree and they want tables check averages to be high. I'm not trying to be a cheapskate I just happen to love eating breakfast sandwiches indoors. Regardless of the reason this rule is absolutely ridiculous. Never in my life have I encountered such nickel-and-diming from a restaurant. Also the last thing you want to hear as a guest is no, and trust me you'll hear a lot of nos at Green Eggs. 

Green Eggs Cafe is byob cash only, but without the reasonable prices usually associated with that mantra. But don't worry, you can always get cash from the strip club style ATM they have glowing in the corner of the dining room...so tacky. It's 2012, we are paying for things with our phones now! Paying the $2.00 ATM fee was the icing on the pancakes for me, no thanks Green Eggs.

I'm really appreciating this diner that never closes. Dependable, variety of dishes and tasty.

#1 fave is the all you can eat soup and salad buffet. It's also served with a choice of warm bread, too

#2 Asian dishes are great!

#3 Quinoa pancakes were so good. Crispy and luscious. It's served with 2 eggs and 2 sausages/bacon. Butter and warm syrup, yumso.

There is also diner seating. Usually quick service and food delivery. Bring check up to cashier. Like the waterfall sounds, too.
